stem:
Farhan knows that $4$ divides $12$ and $4$ divides $20$.

Which two claims keep the direction of the divisibility rule straight?

options.text: Then $4$ divides $12+20$ even if $4$ divides only one of $12$ or $20$.
If $4$ divides a total such as $32$, a split into two addends need not make both addends multiples of $4$.
The same closure holds when $3$ divides $12$ and $5$ divides $20$.

teacher.key_rationale: Same divisor on both starting numbers closes under sum and difference; the reverse split is not forced. Claiming closure from one multiple, or mixing two different divisors, breaks the hinge.
